bug: The earlier probe read Win32_OperatingSystem FreePhysicalMemory and TotalVisibleMemorySize (KB-valued) and treated the numbers as bytes, reporting FreeGB=0.00 / TotalGB=0.00. That was a unit bug, NOT memory exhaustion.

disk_pressure_assessment.not_proven_cause: Low disk space is a plausible contributor to an IO failure, but the observed termination was a console control event, so disk pressure is NOT the cause of this run's termination.
disk_pressure_assessment.reasoning: Free space is critically low on several volumes that the pipeline writes to: C: 13.36 GB (2.81%), E: 6.17 GB (2.2%), H: 16.63 GB (1.78%). A 16-hour import plus cook writes DDC, intermediate assets and saved packages to these volumes.

fix: Values are sourced via PowerShell CIM and converted with kb_to_gb(kb) = kb * 1024 / 1024^3. wmic is unavailable on this host.

memory.method: PowerShell CIM (wmic unavailable on this host)
memory.virtual_free_caveat: FreeVirtualMemory counts the pagefile and can exceed physical RAM. It is NOT physical headroom and must not be used as OOM evidence.

oom_assessment.caveat: No time series was captured during the run, so peak commit is unknown.
oom_assessment.reasoning: Physical RAM 47.75 GB total with 16.778 GB free (35.14%) at probe time. The import ran 16.76 hours, so this single snapshot is not proof about peak usage, but it does refute any claim that the machine was out of memory.
